observation.source_interface: MNCS Environment claims CLI and session event log

outcome.agent_intervention: The session checkout was resumed with --revalidate; the subsequent exact worktree claim succeeded after the selected checkout anchor was refreshed.
outcome.source_level_cause: When the explicit claim target was a different linked worktree, the pre-claim refresh returned early instead of refreshing the selected checkout used as the repository-identity anchor. The stale selected branch/head then caused checkout validation to reject the request before the exact target could be checked.

pressure_hypothesis.title: An explicit worktree claim can be rejected by stale selected-checkout metadata
pressure_hypothesis.subsystem: MNCS Environment claim acquisition and checkout revalidation
pressure_hypothesis.basis: The authentic rejection event records a checkout-validation failure with an explicit branch precondition. Session revalidation refreshed the selected checkout and the subsequent claim succeeded; source inspection and a targeted CLI regression identify the stale selected checkout as the failed anchor when the requested target differs.
pressure_hypothesis.actionable_recommendation: Refresh the selected repository-identity anchor before validating an explicit linked-worktree target, while retaining exact live target branch and checkout checks.
pressure_hypothesis.recurrence: one production incident; recurrence not established
not_measured: total recovery time or tool-call cost
whether other claim failure codes share the same cause
agent intervention reduction after the implementation

measurement_limits: The event does not preserve free-text checkout paths; path-level cause was established by reading the current session snapshot and source code.
The manual revalidation and subsequent successful claim preceded the code change, so they demonstrate a recovery path rather than post-change burden reduction.
This incident is not evidence that all work-claim authorization is defective.
